title: BYD yeni ultra lüks elektrikli sedan modelini test ediyor
summary: BYD'nin üst segment markası Yangwang, Rolls-Royce Phantom benzeri tasarımı ve katı hal batarya teknolojisiyle dikkat çeken yeni lüks elektrikli sedanını test ediyor.
body:
BYD, lüks elektrikli araç segmentindeki iddiasını artırmak için yeni amiral gemisi elektrikli sedan modelini test etmeye başladı. Elektrek'in aktardığına göre, şirketin en üst düzey markası Yangwang çatısı altında geliştirilen ve dahili olarak "HU" adı verilen yeni model, markanın katı hal batarya kullanan ilk elektrikli aracı olacak.

## Öne çıkan tasarım ve teknik detaylar

Çin'de test edilirken görüntülenen araç, Rolls-Royce Phantom modeline benzer tasarımıyla ve BYD'nin ilk arka menteşeli koç kapılarıyla dikkat çekiyor. Yaklaşık 5,5 metre uzunluğa sahip olan bu ultra lüks yönetici sedanı, Mercedes-Benz Maybach S-Class ile benzer boyutlarda üretiliyor. Yerel raporlara ve şirket açıklamalarına göre araç, üst düzey performans sunacak quad-motor e4 platformuyla donatılacak ve megawatt hızlı şarj desteği sunabilecek.

## Fiyat ve çıkış takvimi

BYD henüz resmi fiyatları açıklamasa da, raporlar aracın 2 milyon yuandan, yani yaklaşık 300.000 dolardan daha yüksek bir fiyat etiketine sahip olacağını tahmin ediyor. Yangwang genel müdürü Hu Xiaoqing modelin adının henüz kesinleşmediğini belirtirken, resmi tanıtımın ekim ayında yapılması bekleniyor. Şirket yöneticileri katı hal bataryaların ticari kullanımı için 2027 yılını işaret ediyor.

**Neden önemli?** BYD'nin bu yeni modeli, markanın katı hal batarya teknolojisini ticari araçlarda kullanan ilk üretici olma hedefinin yanı sıra, şirketin geleneksel lüks otomobil üreticilerine elektrikli segmentte meydan okumasını simgeliyor.

source_texts.title: BYD tests new ultra-luxury EV with coach doors and a solid-state battery
source_texts.summary: BYD said the flagship sedan will feature “unprecedented disruptive technology” and will reportedly be the first EV to use its solid-state batteries. more…
source_texts.text:
BYD said the flagship sedan will feature “unprecedented disruptive technology” and will reportedly be the first EV to use its solid-state batteries.
BYD takes on ultra-luxe brands with Yangwang EV sedan
Yangwang is BYD’s highest-end brand with ultra-luxury models ranging from electric hypercars to extreme off-road SUVs.
BYD also uses Yangwang to showcase its breakthrough technologies. In the past, Yangwang vehicles have debuted with disruptive new tech, including BYD’s quad-motor e4 platform, second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging, and its Disus Intelligent Body Control System.
A new Yangwang model was recently spotted testing in China that, according to local reports, will push the brand further into the elite segment.
New images of the vehicle surfaced online, revealing a nearly identical design to the Rolls-Royce Phantom. It will even be BYD’s first vehicle with rear-hinged coach doors.
Hu Xiaoqing, Yangwang’s general manager, shared a few images of the flagship sedan on Weibo and confirmed that the car’s name has yet to be finalized. Internally, BYD is calling it “HU” for now.
The new model is “the culmination of three years of meticulous development by Yangwang, featuring the brand’s signature design language, and is an ultra-luxury executive sedan.”
No other details were revealed, but one image shows the vehicle at BYD’s Flash Charging station, suggesting it can support megawatt fast charging.
According to China’s Autohome, Yangwang’s executive-class EV sedan will be BYD’s first EV to use solid-state batteries among other new technologies.
Zheng Yu, Yangwang’s executive general manager, confirmed the new model will feature “unprecedented disruptive technology,” but didn’t reveal specifics.
The sedan measures about 5.5 meters in length, or about the size of the Mercedes-Benz Maybach S-Class.
BYD executive vice president Stella Li confirmed in an exclusive interview with Carwow.es earlier this month that the company is “in the leading position” in solid-state battery tech and its commercialization.
Li said that BYD will “prove it” with its first vehicle equipped with solid-state batteries set to debut in 2027.
BYD’s battery R&D team is “very strong,” Li said, adding that they are studying the battery chemistry as well as the manufacturing and equipment needed for mass production.
FinDreams, BYD’s battery business, aims to begin producing sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries in limited batches in 2027, scaling up to mass production by 2030.
Will Yangwang’s ultra-luxe sedan be the first to showcase BYD’s solid-state batteries? If it does, it will likely be offered on higher-priced variants, while standard models could still use BYD’s latest Blade LFP batteries.
Top comment by Blake
I expect this will have sold state batteries. The huge sales price means they can afford to ‘hand make’ the batteries and have a high failure rate.
Solid state batteries will matter more when it comes to the inherent complexities of mass production
Outside of that, the flagship model is expected to feature BYD’s quad-motor e4 platform, delivering over 1,000 hp combined.
BYD has yet to announce prices or any details, but reports estimate the Yangwang sedan will cost over 2 million yuan, or nearly $300,000.
The Yangwang U7, the brand’s current luxury electric sedan, starts at just 658,000 yuan ($98,000). According to Autohome, the new executive-class sedan is expected to make its official debut in October, so we should learn more shortly. Check back soon. We’ll keep you updated.
